name: ChatGPT
description: Conversational AI assistant developed by OpenAI for writing, analysis, coding, image understanding, file processing, and task automation. Available on web, iOS, Android, and desktop, with free and paid subscription tiers.
notes: ChatGPT is the consumer-facing product; OpenAI's API platform is cataloged separately. Free plan includes GPT-4o access with rate limits; Plus is \$20/month; Pro is \$200/month. Does not include API access — that is through platform.openai.com.

name: Claude
description: Conversational AI assistant by Anthropic designed for writing, analysis, coding, document review, and research. Accessible via web and mobile; API access is provided separately through the Anthropic Console.
notes: Claude is the consumer product; Anthropic API and specific Claude model releases are cataloged separately. Free plan has usage limits; Claude Pro is \$20/month; Claude Max is \$100–\$200/month.

name: Cursor
description: AI-powered code editor built on VS Code, offering multi-file code editing, codebase-aware chat, AI-powered tab completion, and agent-based coding workflows. Supports multiple frontier LLM backends.
notes: Hobby (free) plan available with limited AI requests. Pro plan is \$20/month with unlimited completions and higher model usage. Business plan is \$40/user/month. The editor itself is a downloadable desktop application; it is not self-hostable in the traditional sense.

name: Perplexity AI
description: AI-powered answer engine that performs real-time web search and synthesizes cited, conversational responses. Supports deep research workflows, file analysis, and model switching for paid users.
notes: Free plan allows basic searches without signup. Pro plan is \$20/month with advanced model selection and higher Pro Search limits. Also offers a Sonar API separately for developer integrations.

name: Midjourney
description: AI image generation platform producing high-quality artistic and photorealistic images from text prompts. Accessible via web interface and Discord. No free tier; requires a paid subscription.
notes: No free trial is currently offered. Plans start at \$10/month (Basic). Discord integration remains available alongside the web app. Stealth mode (private image generation) requires Pro or Mega plan.

name: Runway
description: AI-powered creative platform for text-to-video and image-to-video generation, video editing, background removal, and inpainting. Used by filmmakers and content creators for generative video workflows.
notes: Free plan includes limited credits for video generation. Standard (\$12/month), Pro (\$28/month), and Unlimited (\$76/month) paid plans available. Offers Gen-3 Alpha and Gen-3 Alpha Turbo video generation models via the platform.

name: ElevenLabs
description: AI voice synthesis platform supporting text-to-speech, voice cloning, multilingual speech generation, and audio dubbing. Provides an API for developer integration and a web studio for content creators.
notes: Free plan includes 10,000 credits/month (~10 minutes audio) with non-commercial use only. Starter plan at \$6/month includes commercial license. Professional voice cloning requires Creator plan (\$22/month) or higher. Free-tier output requires attribution.

name: Notion AI
description: AI writing and knowledge management add-on integrated into the Notion workspace. Assists with drafting, summarizing, translating, and querying documents and databases within Notion pages.
notes: Notion AI is an add-on to the Notion workspace, not a standalone product. AI features require a Notion account and the AI add-on (\$10/user/month or \$8/user/month billed annually), on top of the base Notion plan. The base Notion free plan exists; AI requires additional payment.

name: Grammarly
description: AI-powered writing assistant providing grammar checking, style suggestions, tone detection, plagiarism detection, and generative writing features across web browsers, desktop apps, and integrations.
notes: Free plan covers basic grammar and spelling. Premium (\~\$12/month) adds advanced suggestions, tone, and clarity. Business plan targets teams. Available as browser extension, desktop app, and MS Office/Google Docs integration.

name: Jasper
description: AI content platform for marketing teams and enterprises, enabling long-form article writing, campaign copy, social media content, and brand-consistent content generation with customizable brand voice settings.
notes: No permanent free plan; offers a 7-day trial. Creator plan starts at \$39/month. Primarily targets marketing professionals and enterprise content teams. Includes SEO and campaign workflow integrations.

name: Copy.ai
description: AI-powered copywriting and workflow automation platform for marketing teams. Generates sales copy, email sequences, social posts, and marketing content, with GTM (go-to-market) workflow automation features.
notes: Free plan available with limited monthly credits. Pro plan starts at \$36/month. Team and Enterprise plans available with unlimited credits. Increasing focus on GTM workflow automation beyond simple copy generation.

name: Otter.ai
description: AI transcription and meeting assistant that records, transcribes, and summarizes meetings in real-time. Integrates with Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and calendar systems to automate meeting notes.
notes: Free plan includes 300 monthly transcription minutes and limited AI summaries. Pro plan is \$16.99/month with 1,200 minutes and more AI features. Business and Enterprise plans offer advanced controls and integrations.

name: Descript
description: AI-powered audio and video editing platform that treats media as text-based documents. Supports transcript-based editing, AI voice cloning, filler word removal, screen recording, and podcast/video production.
notes: Free plan includes limited transcription and export. Creator (\$24/month) and Business (\$40/month) plans unlock full features. AI voice cloning and overdub features require Creator plan or above.

name: Synthesia
description: AI video generation platform that creates talking-avatar videos from text scripts using over 230 AI avatars and 140+ languages. Used for corporate training, product demos, and marketing videos without filming.
notes: Starter plan at \$29/month with limited video minutes. Creator and Enterprise plans offer more minutes and custom avatar creation. Distinct from open-source video generation tools — fully hosted, no self-hosting option.

name: Gamma
description: AI-powered presentation and document creation tool that generates slides, documents, and web pages from text prompts or outlines. Offers smart formatting, one-click redesign, and publish-to-web capabilities.
notes: Free plan includes limited AI credits (400 on signup). Plus plan at \$8/month and Pro at \$15/month add unlimited AI usage and export options. Outputs web-based presentations, not traditional PPTX by default.

name: v0 by Vercel
description: AI-powered UI generation tool by Vercel that converts text prompts and design descriptions into React/Next.js component code with Tailwind CSS styling. Produces deployment-ready frontend code.
notes: Free tier available with limited monthly credits. Premium plan at \$20/month for higher usage. Developed and operated by Vercel. Output is production-ready React code, typically using shadcn/ui components.

name: Pika
description: AI video generation platform enabling text-to-video and image-to-video creation with motion control, style transfer, and video editing features. Targeted at creators generating short-form social media video content.
notes: Free plan available with limited monthly video generations. Basic (\$8/month), Standard (\$28/month), and Unlimited (\$78/month) paid plans. Pika 2.2 model supports lip sync and motion brush features.

name: GPT-4o
description: OpenAI's flagship multimodal model supporting text, image, audio input and output in a unified architecture. Serves as the primary model powering ChatGPT and is available via API for developers.
notes: GPT-4o is a distinct model from GPT-4 Turbo. Supports native audio and image I/O. Accessible via OpenAI API (usage-based pricing) and via ChatGPT consumer product (separate record). Context window: 128K tokens. Not open-weight; proprietary model.

name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
description: Anthropic's flagship language model offering strong performance across coding, reasoning, instruction-following, and multimodal understanding. Available via API and as the default model powering claude.ai.
notes: Claude 3.5 Sonnet is part of the Claude 3.5 model family. Context window: 200K tokens. Proprietary, closed-weight model. Vision capabilities supported. Claude 3.5 Haiku is a lighter, faster sibling model (cataloged separately if added). Not to be confused with the Claude consumer product (tool:claude).

name: Gemini 1.5 Pro
description: Google DeepMind's long-context multimodal model supporting text, images, audio, video, and code with a 1 million-token context window. Accessible through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.
notes: Gemini 1.5 Pro supports up to 1M token context window (2M in certain API tiers). Proprietary, closed-weight model by Google DeepMind. Available via Gemini API and Google AI Studio. Distinct from Gemini 2.0 Flash and Gemini Ultra variants.

name: DeepSeek-R1
description: Open-weight reasoning model from DeepSeek using reinforcement learning to achieve strong performance on mathematics, coding, and logical reasoning tasks. Weights released under the MIT License.
notes: Released under MIT License — commercial use permitted with broad freedom. DeepSeek-R1 is a 671B MoE model. Distilled variants (e.g., DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B) are smaller, separately available models based on Qwen and Llama architectures. Full R1 requires significant GPU infrastructure; distilled variants run on consumer hardware.

name: Llama 3.1
description: Meta AI's family of open-weight large language models available in 8B, 70B, and 405B parameter sizes with a 128K token context window. Supports multilingual tasks, reasoning, coding, and tool use.
notes: Released under the Llama 3.1 Community License — not a fully OSI-approved open-source license. Commercial use permitted for most developers; entities with >700M MAU must request a separate license from Meta. Download requires signing Meta's license on Hugging Face.

name: Mistral Large
description: Mistral AI's flagship proprietary language model for enterprise use, offering strong multilingual reasoning, coding, and instruction-following performance. Accessible via the Mistral API and La Plateforme.
notes: Mistral Large is a proprietary closed-weight model. Distinct from Mistral's open-weight models such as Mistral 7B and Mixtral 8x7B. Available via the Mistral API (La Plateforme). Context window: 128K tokens.

name: Qwen2.5
description: Alibaba's Qwen2.5 series of open-weight language models available from 0.5B to 72B parameters, with strong performance in coding (Qwen2.5-Coder), mathematics (Qwen2.5-Math), and multilingual instruction following.
notes: Released by Alibaba Cloud under the Qwen License (Apache 2.0 for sub-72B models; larger models have additional commercial terms). Qwen2.5-Coder and Qwen2.5-Math are specialized sub-variants. The 72B model has separate license restrictions for large-scale commercial deployments.

name: FLUX.1 [schnell]
description: Fast text-to-image diffusion model from Black Forest Labs designed for local inference, generating high-quality images in 1–4 steps using Latent Adversarial Diffusion Distillation. Released under Apache 2.0 license.
notes: FLUX.1 [schnell] is the open-source, commercially permissive variant (Apache 2.0). FLUX.1 [dev] uses a non-commercial license and is cataloged separately. FLUX.1 [pro] is proprietary API-only. Schnell is optimized for speed and local inference; 12B parameter model.

name: Whisper
description: Open-source automatic speech recognition model from OpenAI trained on 680,000 hours of multilingual audio data. Supports transcription and translation in 99+ languages. Weights freely available for local use.
notes: Released under the MIT License. Multiple size variants available: tiny, base, small, medium, large, large-v2, large-v3. The OpenAI Whisper API (hosted version) is priced separately at \$0.006/minute. This record covers the open-source model, not the API service.

name: text-embedding-3-large
description: OpenAI's high-performance text embedding model producing dense vector representations for semantic search, RAG, and classification tasks. Outperforms ada-002 on MTEB benchmarks with configurable output dimensions.
notes: Proprietary, closed-weight model. Supports dimensions up to 3072 with shortening capability. Priced at \$0.13/million tokens. API-only; no local execution. text-embedding-3-small is a faster, cheaper sibling model.

name: Stable Diffusion 3.5
description: Stability AI's text-to-image diffusion model featuring improved prompt adherence, image quality, and typography generation. Available in Large (8B) and Medium (2.5B) variants with weights downloadable under a community license.
notes: SD 3.5 weights are available under the Stability AI Community License — free for non-commercial and commercial use with restrictions on large-scale API deployments. Requires acceptance on HuggingFace before download. Architecture: Multimodal Diffusion Transformer (MMDiT).

name: Phi-3
description: Microsoft Research's family of small language models (3.8B–14B parameters) designed for efficient local inference on resource-constrained hardware. Offers strong reasoning performance relative to model size.
notes: Phi-3 Mini (3.8B), Phi-3 Small (7B), and Phi-3 Medium (14B) available. Released under MIT License — commercially permissive. Phi-3.5 and Phi-4 are successor versions. Designed for on-device and edge deployment scenarios.

name: Command R+
description: Cohere's enterprise-focused language model optimized for RAG pipelines, tool use, and multi-step agent workflows. Supports 10+ languages and excels at instruction following for business applications.
notes: Open weights released under Creative Commons NC license (non-commercial for weights). The hosted API via Cohere is commercial and usage-based. Context window: 128K tokens. A successor, Command R+08-2024, was subsequently released.

name: BGE-M3
description: Multi-functionality, multi-linguality, and multi-granularity text embedding model from BAAI. Supports dense retrieval, sparse retrieval, and multi-vector retrieval in 100+ languages. Open-source under MIT License.
notes: Published by BAAI (Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence). Supports dense, sparse (BM25-like), and multi-vector (ColBERT-style) retrieval in a single model. MIT License permits commercial use. Max sequence length: 8192 tokens.

name: Falcon 180B
description: Open-weight large language model from the Technology Innovation Institute with 180 billion parameters, trained on 3.5 trillion tokens of the RefinedWeb dataset. Supports text generation and completion tasks.
notes: Released under the Falcon-180B TII License — allows commercial use with conditions. Requires significant GPU resources for full inference (e.g., multiple A100s or H100s). Falcon 7B and 40B are smaller, more accessible variants. TII is based in Abu Dhabi, UAE.

name: MusicGen
description: Open-source text-to-music and melody-conditioned music generation model from Meta AI AudioCraft. Generates high-quality stereo audio from text descriptions and optional melodic conditioning inputs.
notes: Released under the MIT License. Part of Meta's AudioCraft framework alongside AudioGen. Available in small, medium, and large variants. Runs locally via Python/PyTorch. Distinct from commercial music generation products.

name: LangChain
description: Open-source Python and JavaScript framework for building LLM-powered applications and agents. Provides composable abstractions for chains, tools, memory, and retrieval to streamline AI application development.
notes: Core framework is MIT-licensed and free. LangSmith (observability) and LangGraph Cloud (managed orchestration) are separate commercial products from LangChain Inc. LangGraph (graph-based agent orchestration) is a distinct but closely related project cataloged separately.

name: LlamaIndex
description: Open-source data framework for building RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) applications. Provides data ingestion, indexing, retrieval, and query engines for connecting LLMs to external documents and data sources.
notes: Core framework is MIT-licensed. LlamaCloud is a commercial managed service for production RAG pipelines offered by LlamaIndex (formerly Jerry Liu's company). Formerly known as GPT Index before rebranding to LlamaIndex.

name: Qdrant
description: High-performance vector database and similarity search engine built in Rust for storing, indexing, and querying vector embeddings. Designed for semantic search, RAG, and AI application backends with filtering support.
notes: Core engine is Apache 2.0 licensed and freely self-hostable. Qdrant Cloud is a managed, fully-hosted offering with a free tier (1GB cluster). Supports sparse vectors, payload filtering, and multi-tenancy. Written in Rust for performance and memory safety.

name: Ollama
description: Open-source runtime for running large language models locally on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Exposes an OpenAI-compatible REST API, supports NVIDIA/AMD GPU acceleration, and manages model downloads via a curated library.
notes: MIT-licensed. Supports CUDA (NVIDIA), ROCm (AMD), and Metal (Apple Silicon) acceleration. Modelfile system enables custom model configuration. Provides a Docker image for server deployments. Works with Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, and many other open-weight model families.

name: vLLM
description: High-throughput LLM inference and serving engine using PagedAttention for efficient GPU memory management. Provides OpenAI-compatible APIs, continuous batching, and support for distributed multi-GPU inference.
notes: Apache 2.0 licensed. Key innovation is PagedAttention — a memory management technique enabling 24x higher throughput vs naive implementations. Supports tensor parallelism and pipeline parallelism for multi-GPU deployments. Widely used in production LLM serving.

name: Hugging Face Hub
description: Central platform for hosting, discovering, and sharing AI models, datasets, and Spaces. Provides Git-based model versioning, model cards, inference APIs, and a collaborative ecosystem for the ML community.
notes: Core public model/dataset hosting is free. Pro plan (\$9/month) adds storage and compute credits. Enterprise plan starts at \$50/user/month with SSO, audit logs, and private regions. A self-hosted Enterprise Hub version exists but is distinct from the public platform.

name: Pinecone
description: Fully managed serverless vector database for semantic search, recommendation systems, and RAG applications. Provides automatic scaling, filtered search, and multi-tenancy with pay-per-use billing for reads, writes, and storage.
notes: Fully managed cloud service only — no self-hosting option. Free Starter plan includes 2GB storage and limited usage. Standard production plans have a usage-based pricing model with read units, write units, and storage metering. Transitioned to serverless architecture in 2024.

name: Weaviate
description: Open-source vector database with native multi-modal support, hybrid search (dense + sparse), and built-in ML model integrations. Supports semantic search, question answering, and classification at scale.
notes: Core engine is BSD-3-Clause licensed (open-source). Weaviate Cloud (WCD) is a managed service with a free sandbox tier. Supports GraphQL and REST APIs. Includes built-in vectorizer modules for OpenAI, Cohere, HuggingFace embeddings.

name: LangGraph
description: Graph-based orchestration framework for building stateful multi-step AI agents with fine-grained control over loops, branching, and persistence. Designed for reliable, controllable agentic application workflows.
notes: Developed and maintained by LangChain Inc. MIT-licensed open-source library. LangGraph Cloud is a separate commercial managed deployment product. Distinct from LangChain (cataloged separately) — LangGraph focuses on stateful, cyclical workflows for agents.

name: CrewAI
description: Open-source Python framework for orchestrating autonomous AI agent teams. Enables role-based agent design, task delegation, memory sharing, and tool integration for complex multi-agent collaborative workflows.
notes: Core Python framework is MIT-licensed. CrewAI Enterprise offers managed cloud deployment at custom pricing. Free plan on CrewAI cloud includes ~50 executions/month. Integrates with MCP (Model Context Protocol) and A2A (Agent-to-Agent) communication protocols.

name: Langfuse
description: Open-source LLM observability and tracing platform for debugging, monitoring, and evaluating LLM applications. Provides trace visualization, prompt management, evaluation workflows, and cost analytics.
notes: Core platform is MIT-licensed and self-hostable (via Docker). Langfuse Cloud offers a free Hobby tier (50K traces/month, 30-day retention). Core plan at \$29/month, Pro at \$199/month. Enterprise self-hosted plans available with SSO and advanced RBAC.

name: OpenAI API Platform
description: OpenAI's developer API platform providing programmatic access to GPT-4o, o1, Whisper, DALL·E, Embeddings, and Assistants API. Enables integration of OpenAI models into third-party applications and workflows.
notes: Distinct from the ChatGPT consumer product (tool:chatgpt) and from individual OpenAI models. Pricing is purely usage-based (per-token and per-request). Provides API access to all current OpenAI models including reasoning (o-series), GPT-4o, vision, TTS, ASR, embeddings, and image generation.

name: Anthropic API
description: Anthropic's developer API providing access to Claude model family for text generation, vision, tool use, and document analysis. Offers usage-based token pricing and safety-focused model behavior.
notes: Distinct from Claude consumer product (tool:claude) and individual Claude model records. API access requires signup and payment method. Supports Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku, and Claude 3 Opus. Available on AWS Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI as third-party integrations.

name: llama.cpp
description: C/C++ inference framework for running large language models locally using GGUF quantized model formats. Supports CPU-only inference with optional GPU acceleration on CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, and ROCm backends.
notes: MIT-licensed. Originally created by Georgi Gerganov; repository moved to ggml-org organization. The GGUF model format originated from this project. Foundation for many local LLM tools including Ollama. Supports LLaMA, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen, and many other architectures.

name: Chroma
description: Open-source embedding database for AI applications. Provides a developer-friendly API for storing, querying, and managing embeddings locally or in a client-server deployment, with native Python and JavaScript clients.
notes: Apache 2.0 licensed. Designed primarily for prototyping and local-first development. Chroma Cloud (managed service) is in development. Popular choice for RAG prototyping due to its simple in-memory and persistent local modes. Distinct from Pinecone and Weaviate in its local-first, developer-friendly philosophy.

name: AutoGen
description: Microsoft Research's open-source framework for building event-driven, distributed multi-agent AI systems. Supports asynchronous messaging, agent teams, human-in-the-loop workflows, and cross-language agent communication.
notes: MIT-licensed. AutoGen 0.4 (released 2024) introduced a redesigned asynchronous, event-driven architecture. Supports Python and .NET agents. AutoGen Studio is a no-code UI companion. Distinct from LangGraph and CrewAI in its emphasis on distributed, asynchronous agent communication patterns.

name: Replicate
description: Cloud platform for running AI models via API with pay-per-use pricing. Hosts thousands of open-source and official AI models for image generation, video, language, and audio tasks without infrastructure management.
notes: Pure usage-based pricing — no free tier beyond an initial credit allowance. Billing by hardware-seconds (for community models) or by output units (for official models). Cog is Replicate's open-source tool for packaging custom models. Supports private model deployment with autoscaling.

name: GitHub Copilot
description: AI-assisted pair programmer by GitHub and OpenAI that provides context-aware autocomplete suggestions, chat-based code explanations, automated unit test generation, and CLI terminal command assistance directly within popular code editors.
notes: Provides a free tier with monthly limits for individual developers and free access for verified students. Copilot Pro is $10/month; Business is $19/user/month; Enterprise is $39/user/month. Integrates across VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs, and Neovim.

name: Windsurf
description: Agentic AI-native IDE created by Codeium featuring Cascade, an autonomous coding agent. Performs multi-file code refactoring, context-aware command execution, real-time codebase indexing, and multi-line tab completions.
notes: Native desktop client runs locally; AI agent reasoning and indexing connect to cloud inference. Free plan includes unlimited completions and limited Cascade agent prompts. Pro plan is $15–$20/month. Built on open-source VS Code fork.

name: Suno
description: Generative AI music creation platform that produces full-length songs with vocals, instruments, lyrics, and arrangements from natural language prompts. Enables genres from pop and rock to classical and hip-hop.
notes: Basic plan offers 50 free credits daily (10 songs) for non-commercial use. Pro ($10/month) and Premier ($30/month) plans include commercial rights and priority generation queues. Models include v3 and v3.5.

name: Udio
description: AI music creation service founded by former Google DeepMind researchers that synthesizes expressive vocal tracks, intricate musical compositions, and stem separations from descriptive text prompts with granular section-by-section editing.
notes: Free tier grants monthly credits with standard audio quality. Standard plan ($10/month) and Pro plan ($30/month) unlock stem downloads, extended track generation, and commercial rights.

name: Lovable
description: Full-stack AI application builder that turns plain English descriptions into complete web applications with front-end UI, backend logic, authentication, and database connections, accompanied by live preview and GitHub synchronization.
notes: Free tier offers daily generation credits. Paid subscriptions provide expanded editing credits, custom domains, and direct production deployments. Integrates natively with Supabase for data persistence and authentication.

name: Bolt.new
description: In-browser AI development environment powered by WebContainers that prompts, executes, tests, and deploys full-stack Node.js and web applications entirely inside the browser without requiring local machine installations.
notes: Created by StackBlitz. Runs Node.js runtimes client-side in the browser via WebAssembly. Free tier offers daily token limits; Pro plans provide larger context windows and higher concurrency.

name: Replit Agent
description: Autonomous AI coding agent embedded in Replit that plans, writes, debugs, and provisions full-stack software applications from high-level natural language specifications, handling database setup, backend APIs, and cloud hosting.
notes: Requires Replit Core subscription ($20/month or $240/year) or token add-on credits. Autonomous agent inspects environment errors, runs shell commands, and automatically installs package dependencies.

name: Devin
description: Autonomous AI software engineering agent developed by Cognition that navigates complex codebases, resolves GitHub issues, writes tests, runs terminal commands in sandboxed environments, and creates pull requests end-to-end.
notes: Designed to operate as a full autonomous developer rather than a mere code autocomplete tool. Operates inside isolated virtual machines with dedicated shell, browser, and editor access. Requires paid subscription or enterprise contract.

name: HeyGen
description: AI video generation platform that produces studio-quality talking avatar videos, multilingual video translations with lip-sync matching, and personalized marketing videos from text scripts and audio recordings.
notes: Free tier includes 1 credit (up to 1 minute of video). Creator ($29/month) and Business ($89/month) tiers provide unlimited video generation, 4K rendering, and custom instant avatar training.

name: Krea AI
description: Real-time visual generation and enhancement tool featuring instant canvas drawing-to-image synthesis, video generation, AI upscaling, and motion video controls for digital artists, designers, and creative directors.
notes: Free tier allows daily generation runs with standard queue priority. Basic ($30/month), Pro ($60/month), and Max ($120/month) plans offer real-time generation speeds, commercial rights, and high-resolution upscaling.

name: Leonardo.Ai
description: Generative AI creative production platform offering fine-tuned image generation models, real-time canvas editing, texture generation for 3D assets, and graphic design tooling for game developers and marketing artists.
notes: Acquired by Canva in 2024. Free tier provides 150 daily generation tokens. Apprentice ($12/month), Artisan ($30/month), and Maestro ($60/month) plans unlock proprietary models like Leonardo Phoenix, custom model training, and privacy mode.

name: Julius AI
description: AI-powered data analysis assistant that interprets spreadsheets, CSVs, and SQL databases. Generates Python scripts in an internal sandbox to render publication-ready charts, perform statistical models, and draft analytical reports.
notes: Free tier allows up to 15 computational queries per month. Basic ($20/month) and Pro ($45/month) tiers grant higher message quotas, multi-file uploads, and longer sandbox compute execution time.

name: Poe
description: Consumer AI platform created by Quora providing unified access to multiple frontier and open-weight models including Claude, GPT-4o, Gemini, and FLUX, enabling users to create, share, and monetize custom prompt bots.
notes: Offers daily compute points on the free tier. Paid subscription ($19.99/month or $199.99/year) grants 1 million monthly compute points for heavy access to premier foundation models. Features creator revenue sharing.

name: Phind
description: AI search engine and coding answer platform tailored for software developers. Crawls technical documentation, Stack Overflow threads, and GitHub repositories to synthesize verified, executable code solutions with source links.
notes: Free access without account for standard searches. Phind Pro ($20/month) unlocks advanced reasoning models, longer context lengths, and enhanced VS Code extension features.

name: Harvey
description: Enterprise AI platform purpose-built for law firms and corporate legal departments. Automates contract analysis, regulatory compliance auditing, legal research synthesis, and due diligence with strict enterprise data segregation.
notes: Backed by OpenAI Startup Fund and Sequoia. Strictly commercial enterprise pricing negotiated per seat. No public free tier or open trial. Enforces strict zero-data-retention confidentiality policies.

name: Beautiful.ai
description: Cloud-based presentation tool using smart design rules and AI generation to automatically adapt slide layouts as content is added. Converts text outlines into finished slide decks with professional typography and color palettes.
notes: Requires paid subscription after 14-day trial. Pro plan is $12/month (annual billing); Team plan is $40/user/month. Distinct from Gamma by focusing on traditional corporate widescreen slide dimensions and enterprise templates.

name: Tome
description: AI-native storytelling workspace that generates multimedia narratives, presentations, and product teardowns. Combines generated copy, relevant AI imagery, interactive prototypes, and web embeds on flexible dynamic canvases.
notes: Free tier provides initial compute credits for personal decks. Professional plan ($16/month) and Enterprise plans offer unlimited AI generation, custom branding, and PDF export capabilities.

name: OpenAI o1
description: OpenAI's frontier reasoning model designed to spend inference time thinking before producing answers. Uses reinforcement learning to execute long chain-of-thought reasoning across competitive math, coding, and scientific research benchmarks.
notes: Includes full o1 and lighter o1-mini variants. Available via OpenAI API (usage-based token billing) and ChatGPT Plus/Pro. Chains of thought are hidden from users; summary reasoning tokens are billed as part of output.

name: Gemma 2
description: Family of lightweight open-weight models (2.6B, 9B, and 27B parameters) from Google DeepMind built upon Gemini research. Features sliding-window attention and knowledge distillation for exceptional single-GPU efficiency.
notes: Distributed under the permissive Gemma Terms of Use allowing commercial development. Trained on up to 13 trillion tokens. Available in Base and Instruct (IT) variants across standard 8K context windows.

name: Claude 3.5 Haiku
description: Anthropic's fastest language model in the Claude 3.5 family. Delivers coding, text analysis, and instruction-following performance matching prior flagship Claude 3 Opus at high inference speeds and low per-token operational cost.
notes: Proprietary closed model. Features 200K token context window. Highly suited for customer-facing chatbots, rapid code review, and high-volume background processing pipelines.

name: DeepSeek-V3
description: Open-weight 671-billion parameter Mixture-of-Experts language model (activating 37B parameters per token) developed by DeepSeek. Features Multi-head Latent Attention and auxiliary-loss-free load balancing for cost-effective inference.
notes: Weights released under the DeepSeek Model License allowing commercial use and distillation. Context window: 128K tokens. Acts as the base model from which DeepSeek-R1 was trained.

name: Llama 3.2
description: Meta's multimodal open-weight collection offering 11B and 90B vision-language models alongside 1B and 3B lightweight edge text models. Optimized for mobile, on-device computing, and visual document analysis across 128K context windows.
notes: Released under Llama 3.2 Community License. Requires license acceptance on Hugging Face. 1B and 3B models run on Qualcomm and MediaTek mobile chipsets; 11B and 90B handle image-text reasoning.

name: Codestral
description: Mistral AI's 22-billion parameter open-weight language model trained on 80+ programming languages. Features a 32K context window with fill-in-the-middle capabilities for IDE autocompletions and codebase refactoring.
notes: Distributed under the Mistral Non-Production License for research and testing; commercial usage requires licensing through Mistral API or cloud partners. Distinct from general-purpose Mistral models.

name: Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2)
description: Meta FAIR's foundation model for real-time visual promptable object segmentation across both static images and dynamic video frames, tracking target object masks continuously through occlusions and camera perspective shifts.
notes: Code and model weights released under the permissive Apache 2.0 License allowing commercial utilization. Features interactive prompting via clicks, bounding boxes, or freeform mask inputs.

name: DINOv2
description: Vision foundation model developed by Meta FAIR using self-supervised learning without text supervision. Produces universal visual features for monocular depth estimation, semantic segmentation, and image retrieval.
notes: Released under Apache 2.0 license. Available in ViT-S, ViT-B, ViT-L, and ViT-g parameter sizes. Delivers dense visual descriptors directly usable by linear classifiers without fine-tuning.

name: CLIP
description: OpenAI's foundational vision-language model trained on 400 million image-text pairs via contrastive learning. Maps images and text into a shared embedding space to enable zero-shot image classification and semantic multimodal search.
notes: Released under MIT License. Serves as the fundamental vision-text alignment backbone powering Stable Diffusion guidance, DALL-E priors, and multimodal vector databases.

name: HunyuanVideo
description: Tencent's 13-billion parameter open-source video generation model utilizing a unified dual-stream and single-stream diffusion transformer. Generates high-definition (720p/1080p) cinema-grade video clips with physical dynamics.
notes: Released under Apache 2.0 license for code and Tencent Hunyuan Community License for weights. Supports high-fidelity 54-frame video clips. ComfyUI workflow wrappers widely adopted by local AI communities.

name: CogVideoX
description: Open-source text-to-video diffusion transformer model developed by THUDM and Zhipu AI. Employs 3D Variational Autoencoders and expert transformer backends to produce coherent 6-second video clips up to 4K resolution.
notes: Available in 2B and 5B parameter sizes under Apache 2.0 and custom community licensing. Features prompt refinement via integrated vision-language processing.

name: Voyage-3
description: High-performance text embedding model engineered by Voyage AI delivering top retrieval accuracy on the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB). Optimized for domain-specific RAG pipelines across finance, code, and legal documents.
notes: Proprietary cloud model accessed via REST API. Context length: 32,000 tokens with 1024-dimensional outputs. Official default embedding partner for Anthropic Claude integrations.

name: Cohere Embed v3
description: Cohere's enterprise embedding model family supporting 100+ languages and multimodal image-text searches. Outperforms previous generations in noisy document retrieval using compression-aware quantization embeddings.
notes: Cloud API model offering `embed-english-v3.0` and `embed-multilingual-v3.0`. Supports int8 and binary embedding outputs to shrink vector database memory footprints by up to 90%.

name: XTTS-v2
description: Deep learning text-to-speech foundation model from Coqui capable of realistic voice cloning across 17 languages from a 3-second audio reference sample without extensive speaker fine-tuning.
notes: Released under the Coqui Public Model License (CPML), which permits non-commercial and research use while requiring licensing for commercial distribution. Community maintenance ongoing via open-source forks.

name: Mistral NeMo
description: 12-billion parameter multilingual foundation model co-developed by Mistral AI and NVIDIA. Features a 128K context window and the Tekken tokenizer for efficient multilingual inference and code synthesis.
notes: Released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license. Drop-in replacement for systems utilizing Mistral 7B with significantly improved reasoning and multi-language fluency.

name: Jina Embeddings v3
description: Open-source 570M parameter embedding model supporting 8192-token context lengths across 89 languages. Uses task-specific LoRA adapters to optimize vectors for retrieval, classification, clustering, and semantic matching.
notes: Weights published under CC-BY-NC 4.0; commercial use available via Jina AI API platform. Features 5 distinct task-tailored vector spaces through dynamic adapter routing.

name: Model Context Protocol SDK
subtype: Open Agent Protocol Specification and SDK
description: Open standard and software development kit introduced by Anthropic that standardizes how AI applications and agents securely access external context, enterprise databases, file systems, and API tools over JSON-RPC.
notes: MIT-licensed open standard. Eliminates custom point-to-point integrations by providing reusable server and client abstractions implemented across Python, TypeScript, and Kotlin.

name: LiteLLM
description: Open-source AI proxy and gateway that unifies calls to 100+ LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, Ollama) using the standard OpenAI input-output format, handling load balancing, fallbacks, and cost tracking.
notes: Core proxy is MIT-licensed. LiteLLM Enterprise offers dedicated virtual key management, SSO, rate limits, and custom billing dashboards for production deployments.

name: SGLang
subtype: Fast Serving Engine & Structured Decoding Framework
description: High-throughput serving engine and programming language for large language models. Optimizes complex prompt workflows, multi-turn chat loops, and constrained JSON decodings with RadixAttention KV-cache reuse.
notes: Apache 2.0 licensed. Developed by researchers from LMSYS and UC Berkeley. RadixAttention retains KV-caches across multiple API calls, significantly speeding up complex reasoning and agent workflows.

name: TensorRT-LLM
description: Open-source Python and C++ inference optimization library engineered by NVIDIA. Compiles and executes large language models with kernel fusions, in-flight batching, FP8 quantization, and multi-GPU tensor parallelism.
notes: Released under the Apache 2.0 license. Powers NVIDIA NIM microservices. Maximizes token throughput and minimizes first-token latency on NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200) and Blackwell hardware architectures.

name: Unsloth
description: High-speed, memory-efficient fine-tuning library for open-weight models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma). Uses custom hand-written GPU Triton kernels to speed up LoRA and QLoRA training by up to 5x while reducing VRAM usage by 80%.
notes: Core software open-source under Apache 2.0. Unsloth Pro and Enterprise provide multi-GPU distributed fine-tuning and commercial support. Enables fine-tuning large 70B parameter models on modest GPU configurations.

name: Axolotl
description: Config-driven tool designed to streamline the post-training and fine-tuning of foundation language models. Supports full fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, DPO, and PPO via simple YAML configurations across multi-GPU setups.
notes: Apache 2.0 licensed. Supports FlashAttention, xFormers, DeepSpeed, and FSDP natively. Serves as a standard training harness for open-source AI researchers and community model builders.

name: DSPy
description: Stanford University's open-source framework for programmatically optimizing language model prompts and weights. Replaces brittle hand-written prompt templates with modular Python signatures that are compiled and auto-tuned algorithmically.
notes: MIT-licensed. Treats LLM pipelines as parameterized programs with automated optimizers (Teleprompters / MIPRO) that systematically discover high-performing few-shot demonstrations and prompt variations.

name: OpenRouter
description: Unified API gateway that aggregates hundreds of proprietary and open-weight AI models through a single OpenAI-compatible interface, offering automated fallback routing, competitive per-token pricing, and transparent latency benchmarks.
notes: Purely usage-based without subscriptions; charges exact upstream provider costs plus minimal transaction margins. Supports crypto and fiat credit top-ups. Includes a free tier for select open-source models.

name: Together AI
description: High-performance cloud platform providing fast API inference for open-source AI models, dedicated GPU compute clusters, and custom model fine-tuning environments with enterprise SOC 2 compliance.
notes: Billed on per-token consumption for serverless endpoints and per-hour rates for dedicated H100 GPU clusters. Known for high token-per-second inference speeds powered by custom flash-attention kernels.

name: Groq Cloud
description: Ultra-fast AI inference platform powered by custom Language Processing Unit (LPU) semiconductor hardware. Serves open-weight LLMs, vision, and Whisper transcription models at hundreds of tokens per second with near-instant response times.
notes: Provides a free tier with daily rate limits. Paid Pay-As-You-Go tier charges standard per-million-token consumption. LPU deterministic architecture avoids typical GPU queuing jitter, enabling real-time conversational voice agents.

name: Modal
subtype: Serverless Cloud Compute Platform for AI
description: Serverless cloud infrastructure platform that allows developers to run Python code, containerized AI workloads, batch model inference, and fine-tuning jobs on cloud GPUs with sub-second cold starts and per-second billing.
notes: Includes $30/month in free compute credits for all users. Billed strictly by execution seconds across CPU, memory, and GPU (T4, A10G, L4, A100, H100) allocations. Container environments are defined directly in native Python code.

name: RunPod
subtype: Distributed Cloud GPU & Serverless AI Platform
description: Cloud computing provider specializing in affordable GPU rental pods, distributed training clusters, and serverless AI worker endpoints for deploying inference APIs, image generators, and machine learning models globally.
notes: Offers Secure Cloud (Tier 3/4 data centers) and Community Cloud (budget pricing). Billed by the minute/second. Serverless GPU endpoints automatically scale to zero when idle to save infrastructure costs.

name: Braintrust
description: Enterprise evaluation, tracing, and prompt-engineering platform for LLM applications. Provides CI/CD regression testing, dataset curation, automated scoring, real-time production monitoring, and prompt playground environments.
notes: Free plan includes unlimited seats and a monthly allotment of evaluation records and traces. Pro plan ($50/month) and Enterprise plans offer custom retention, SSO, private cloud deployments, and dedicated support.

name: Arize Phoenix
description: Open-source AI observability library and dashboard for tracing LLM execution steps, evaluating RAG retrieval pipelines, troubleshooting hallucination rates, and benchmarking agent execution graphs using OpenTelemetry standards.
notes: Released under Apache 2.0 license. Can be run entirely locally inside a Jupyter notebook or Docker container without transmitting telemetry to third-party clouds. Arize Cloud provides managed SaaS hosting.

name: Guardrails AI
description: Open-source Python and JavaScript framework that enforces structural guarantees, type safety, PII redaction, toxicity filtering, and prompt injection defense on LLM inputs and outputs using community-authored validators.
notes: Core framework is Apache 2.0 licensed. Operates Guardrails Hub, a marketplace of pre-built validators (regex matching, hallucination detection, schema compliance). Guardrails Server provides a containerized microservice API.

name: pgvector
subtype: Vector Similarity Search Extension for PostgreSQL
description: Open-source vector similarity search extension for PostgreSQL. Stores exact and approximate nearest-neighbor vector embeddings alongside relational relational records using HNSW and IVFFlat indexing methods.
notes: Distributed under the PostgreSQL License. Widely deployed across AWS RDS, Supabase, Neon, Azure PostgreSQL, and self-hosted database clusters to consolidate vectors and transactional data in a single ACID engine.

name: LanceDB
description: Developer-friendly, serverless open-source vector database built on the columnar Lance data format. Supports disk-native vector search, multi-modal storage, hybrid retrieval, and zero-infrastructure local embedding storage.
notes: Apache 2.0 licensed. Can run serverlessly in-process (like DuckDB or SQLite) embedded directly in Python/Node applications, querying disk and object storage (S3/GCS) without dedicated database servers. LanceDB Cloud offers enterprise managed hosting.

name: Character.ai
description: Consumer conversational AI platform hosting millions of user-created personas, fictional characters, historical figures, and interactive roleplay bots powered by custom large language models optimized for engaging multi-turn dialogue.
notes: Co-founded by former Google Brain researchers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas. Free tier includes community bot interactions. c.ai+ subscription ($9.99/month) offers priority queue access, faster response speeds, and early feature previews.

name: QuillBot
description: AI writing enhancement tool offering multi-mode sentence paraphrasing, grammar checking, summarization, citation generation, and plagiarism detection to improve vocabulary, readability, and academic writing fluency.
notes: Free tier allows standard paraphrasing up to 125 words at a time. Premium subscription ($9.95/month or $4.17/month billed annually) unlocks unlimited word paraphrasing, tone comparisons, and full plagiarism scans.

name: Adobe Firefly
description: Creative generative AI suite developed by Adobe trained exclusively on licensed content from Adobe Stock and public domain assets, powering text-to-image, generative fill, text effects, and vector recoloring inside Adobe Creative Cloud.
notes: Explicitly engineered for commercial safety with enterprise intellectual property indemnification. Free Adobe accounts receive 25 generative credits monthly; Premium plans and Creative Cloud subscriptions grant larger monthly allotments.

name: Canva Magic Studio
description: Suite of generative design features embedded across the Canva ecosystem, including Magic Media (text-to-image/video), Magic Expand, Magic Eraser, Magic Switch (multi-format document conversion), and AI copy generation.
notes: Included natively within Canva accounts. Free users get a lifetime allocation of 50 AI queries; Canva Pro ($15/month or $120/year) and Canva Teams unlock 500 uses per month per user.

name: Fireflies.ai
description: AI meeting assistant that joins video conference calls (Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Webex) to record audio, produce searchable timestamped transcripts, extract action items, and generate executive recaps with CRM integrations.
notes: Free tier includes unlimited transcription with 800 minutes of cloud storage. Pro ($10/seat/month) and Business ($19/seat/month) unlock unlimited storage, AI summary generation, smart search filters, and CRM sync.

name: Superhuman AI
description: AI-accelerated email client for Gmail and Outlook that writes complete email drafts matching personal tone, summarizes lengthy email threads in one sentence, corrects phrasing, and automates inbox triage with keyboard shortcuts.
notes: Strictly paid premium productivity service starting at $30/user/month (Starter) or $45/user/month (Growth). AI features analyze past sent email history locally/privately to emulate personal writing habits.

name: Mem.ai
description: Self-organizing AI workspace that connects personal notes, web clips, meeting minutes, and document files without requiring manual tagging or hierarchical folders, using semantic search to surface relevant past context.
notes: Free tier provides basic note storage and search. Mem Plus ($14.99/month or $10/month annually) unlocks unlimited Chat with Mem, larger document upload limits, and smart organization features.

name: Luma Dream Machine
description: AI video generation system built by Luma AI that transforms text and image inputs into realistic 5-second video shots with accurate physics, coherent motion, character consistency, and dynamic camera movements.
notes: Free tier includes 30 generations per month with standard processing queues. Standard ($29.99/month), Pro ($99.99/month), and Premier ($499.99/month) tiers offer commercial rights, priority queues, and higher resolution.

name: Kling AI
description: High-definition video generation platform developed by Kuaishou capable of rendering cinematic videos up to 2 minutes long at 1080p resolution and 30fps with advanced physical simulation and 3D spatio-temporal attention.
notes: Free tier grants daily login credits for generating short clips. Standard, Pro, and Premier subscriptions provide higher credit quotas, longer video extensions, motion brush features, and watermark removal.

name: Speechify
description: AI text-to-speech reading application that converts books, PDFs, online articles, and documents into natural humanlike speech at speeds up to 4.5x, featuring celebrity voice models, OCR document scanning, and cross-device sync.
notes: Free version offers 10 standard reading voices. Speechify Premium ($139/year) unlocks 30+ natural AI voices, 60+ languages, note-taking, and optical character recognition for physical books. Offers Speechify Studio for creators.

name: Scribe
description: AI productivity tool that records desktop browser workflows and automatically converts click sequences and keystrokes into visual step-by-step how-to guides, screenshots, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
notes: Free Basic plan allows unlimited guide creation in web browsers. Pro plan ($23/seat/month) supports desktop application recording, automated screenshot redaction, custom branding, and export to PDF/HTML.

name: Consensus
description: AI-powered search engine for scientific research that queries over 200 million peer-reviewed journal papers. Synthesizes scientific consensus meters, extracts study findings, and provides citations without hallucinating academic evidence.
notes: Powered by Semantic Scholar database. Free tier includes basic searches and limited AI Consensus Meters. Premium tier ($8.99/month billed annually) provides unlimited GPT-4 synthesis, study quality filters, and Zotero integration.

name: Elicit
description: AI research assistant that automates scientific literature reviews. Searches academic papers, extracts structured data columns (sample size, methodologies, outcomes), and summarizes research questions with direct source attribution.
notes: Basic plan provides 5,000 one-time research credits. Plus ($10/month) and Enterprise plans grant recurring monthly credits, high-speed multi-paper data extraction, and RIS citation exports.

name: Glean
description: Enterprise search and work assistant that indexes internal company tools (Slack, Google Drive, Jira, GitHub, Salesforce) to answer employee questions, synthesize company knowledge, and build internal conversational agents with enterprise permissions.
notes: Enterprise B2B software with custom per-seat pricing. Enforces real-time ACL (Access Control List) checks ensuring employees only see internal information they have existing corporate permissions to view.

name: CodeRabbit
description: AI-powered code review platform that integrates into GitHub and GitLab pull requests. Provides line-by-line code feedback, detects edge cases and security vulnerabilities, generates release summaries, and answers questions in PR comments.
notes: 100% free for open-source repositories without limits. Pro plan ($15/developer/month) provides automated reviews on private repositories, custom prompt instructions, and CI workflow integrations.

name: Tabnine
description: Privacy-first AI code completion and chat assistant for software engineers. Offers contextual autocompletions and codebase querying trained exclusively on open-source code with permissive licenses, deployable on-premises or private clouds.
notes: Starter plan is free with basic completions. Pro plan ($12/user/month) adds whole-line and full-function completions. Enterprise plan ($39/user/month) allows self-hosted on-premises deployment, private fine-tuning, and zero data leakage guarantees.

name: Make
description: Visual no-code integration platform that connects hundreds of cloud applications and databases. Features native AI modules for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Hugging Face to build automated multi-step data pipelines and business processes.
notes: Formerly known as Integromat. Free tier allows 1,000 monthly operations with 2 active scenarios. Core ($9/month) and Pro ($16/month) tiers increase operation quotas, execution frequency, and custom webhook rates.

name: Gemini 1.5 Flash
description: Google DeepMind's lightweight, low-latency multimodal foundation model. Optimized for high-frequency tasks, cost efficiency, and massive 1-million-token context processing across text, audio, images, and video feeds.
notes: Accessible via Google AI Studio (with a free tier) and Google Cloud Vertex AI. Distilled from Gemini 1.5 Pro to deliver sub-second time-to-first-token for high-volume multimodal applications.

name: GPT-4o mini
description: OpenAI's cost-efficient small multimodal model replacing GPT-3.5 Turbo. Supports text and vision inputs with a 128K context window, scoring strongly on reasoning, coding, and mathematical benchmarks at a fraction of flagship model costs.
notes: Priced at $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output tokens. Powers standard free-tier interactions in ChatGPT and high-volume background API workloads.

name: Qwen2.5-Coder
description: Code-specialized open-weight model series from Alibaba Cloud ranging from 0.5B to 32B parameters. Trained on 5.5 trillion tokens of source code, technical documentation, and synthetic coding datasets with a 128K context window.
notes: Flagship 32B model matches GPT-4o on major code evaluation benchmarks (EvalPlus, MultiPL-E). Released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license for unrestricted commercial use.

name: Qwen2-VL
description: Vision-language model family from Alibaba (2B, 7B, 72B) featuring NaViT dynamic image resolution architecture. Accurately reads arbitrary aspect-ratio images, interprets fine document text, and parses video events with second-level grounding.
notes: 2B and 7B models released under Apache 2.0; 72B model uses the Qwen License. Processes high-definition documents, scans, charts, and 20+ minute video clips seamlessly without fixed grid distortion.

name: DeepSeek-Coder-V2
description: Open-source Mixture-of-Experts language model for code and mathematics supporting 338 programming languages and a 128K context window. Available in 16B (2.4B active) and 236B (21B active) parameter scales.
notes: Released under the MIT License for the Lite version and DeepSeek License for the 236B version. Demonstrates competitive performance with closed frontier models on HumanEval and MBPP.

name: Pixtral 12B
description: 12-billion parameter multimodal language model trained by Mistral AI. Integrates a custom 400M parameter vision encoder to natively reason over arbitrary images, documents, and technical charts alongside natural text across a 128K context window.
notes: Released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license. Retains state-of-the-art text understanding capabilities from Mistral NeMo while adding zero-shot diagram and document reading abilities.

name: FLUX.1 [dev]
description: 12-billion parameter open-weight rectified flow transformer model from Black Forest Labs. Delivers state-of-the-art text-to-image quality, photorealistic skin textures, accurate multi-word typography, and detailed prompt comprehension.
notes: Distributed under the FLUX.1 [dev] Non-Commercial License for research and personal use. Direct guidance-distilled version of FLUX.1 [pro] yielding competitive image fidelity in approximately 28–50 sampling steps.

name: Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL)
description: Stability AI's flagship 3.5-billion parameter latent diffusion model engineered for native 1024x1024 resolution image generation. Uses a base model followed by an ensemble refiner model to render intricate backgrounds and realistic lighting.
notes: Released under the CreativeML OpenRAIL++-M License allowing commercial deployment. Extremely broad ecosystem of community fine-tunes, LoRA checkpoints, ControlNets, and ComfyUI workflows.

name: Kolors
description: Open-source text-to-image diffusion model developed by Kuaishou's Kolors Team. Built with the ChatGLM language model as its text encoder to achieve nuanced bilingual understanding (Chinese and English) and high-quality typography rendering.
notes: Code released under Apache 2.0; model weights distributed under the Kolors Community License allowing commercial use after registration. Highly praised for photorealistic human portraits and Asian cultural aesthetics.

name: Bark
description: Transformer-based text-to-audio foundation model created by Suno. Generates realistic multilingual speech, non-verbal vocalizations (laughter, sighs, clearing throat), background ambient sounds, and basic music from text prompts.
notes: Released under the MIT License for open commercial use. Uses EnCodec tokens and GPT-style autoregressive transformers rather than conventional acoustic spectrogram models.

name: Whisper large-v3-turbo
description: Fine-tuned, pruned variant of OpenAI's Whisper large-v3 model. Reduces the number of decoder layers from 32 to 4 to deliver an 8x speedup in multilingual audio transcription and translation with minimal loss in accuracy.
notes: MIT-licensed open-source model. Optimized for real-time edge speech recognition pipelines, live call transcription, and low-latency audio processing servers.

name: BGE Reranker-v2
description: Multilingual cross-encoder reranking model series (m3 and gemma variants) developed by the Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence. Computes deep relevance scores between queries and retrieved passages to dramatically boost RAG precision.
notes: MIT License allows commercial applications. Applied as a second-stage reranker after initial bi-encoder vector search in retrieval pipelines to re-score candidate documents.

name: Cohere Rerank 3
description: Enterprise cross-encoder foundation model from Cohere engineered for semantic reranking of search results across 100+ languages, semi-structured JSON objects, emails, code snippets, and noisy web documents.
notes: Cloud API accessed via `rerank-v3.5`. Supports context lengths up to 4096 tokens per document chunk. Integrates with Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Pinecone, and Qdrant search stacks.

name: InternVL 2.0
description: Open-source multimodal foundation model family developed by OpenGVLab ranging from 1B to 108B parameters. Achieves top scores in multimodal benchmarks, chart understanding, OCR, document analysis, and video grounding.
notes: Released under Apache 2.0 license for code and model weights. Features dynamic image tiling allowing high-resolution inputs (up to 4K) without downsampling degradation.

name: Molmo 72B
description: Open multimodal vision-language model developed by the Allen Institute for AI (Ai2). Outperforms proprietary models on academic benchmarks using open datasets and transparent human-collected visual pointing annotations.
notes: Built using Qwen2-72B as the base LLM combined with an open CLIP vision backbone. Weights released under Apache 2.0 alongside open training code, evaluation harnesses, and datasets.

name: Moondream2
description: Compact 1.6-billion parameter vision-language model engineered to run locally on edge hardware, mobile phones, and Raspberry Pi devices. Capable of visual question answering, image captioning, and object detection.
notes: Apache 2.0 licensed. Combines SigLIP visual embeddings with the Phi-1.5 language model to deliver real-time visual reasoning with negligible RAM and compute footprint.

name: Milvus
description: Open-source cloud-native distributed vector database designed to manage and search tens of billions of vector embeddings in milliseconds. Built with decoupled storage and compute for massive enterprise scale.
notes: Graduated LF AI & Data Foundation project under Apache 2.0. Zilliz Cloud provides the fully managed enterprise cloud edition. Supports HNSW, IVF, and GPU-accelerated indexes (Knowhere).

name: Faiss
description: Open-source C++ and Python library developed by Meta Fundamental AI Research for efficient dense vector clustering and similarity search across billion-scale datasets with complete GPU acceleration and quantization support.
notes: MIT-licensed. Foundational low-level algorithm library underlying many production vector databases and retrieval systems. Features Product Quantization (PQ) and Inverted File (IVF) indexes.

name: Haystack
description: Production-ready open-source Python framework from deepset for constructing customizable RAG pipelines, semantic search engines, and agent workflows using a typed, directed acyclic graph (DAG) component architecture.
notes: Apache 2.0 licensed. Haystack 2.0 features modular component connections, flexible document store adapters, and seamless integration with deepset Cloud for enterprise deployments.

name: txtai
description: Open-source all-in-one embeddings database that combines vector indexing, relational SQL storage, document extraction, and graph networks to power semantic search, knowledge graphs, and LLM orchestration.
notes: Apache 2.0 licensed. Developed by NeuML. Enables querying multimodal data and knowledge graphs using standard SQL syntax combined with vector similarity matching.

name: RAGFlow
description: Open-source RAG engine based on deep document understanding. Extracts and parses unstructured data from complex multi-column PDFs, financial tables, slides, and scanned forms with vision-based document layout analysis.
notes: Apache 2.0 licensed by InfiniFlow. Solves the "garbage in, garbage out" challenge in RAG by visualizing document chunks and preserving tabular structure across multi-page corporate PDFs.

name: Microsoft GraphRAG
description: Modular RAG pipeline developed by Microsoft Research that extracts structured knowledge graphs and entity communities from unstructured text documents, enabling holistic global summarization over entire private corpuses.
notes: MIT-licensed. Addresses standard vector RAG's failure to answer query-focused global questions (e.g., "What are the major themes across all 50 reports?") by leveraging hierarchical Leiden community detection.

name: Dify
description: Open-source platform combining Backend-as-a-Service and visual workflow orchestration for AI applications. Enables teams to visually build multi-agent systems, complex RAG pipelines, and API integrations with one-click deployment.
notes: Open-source under Apache 2.0 with commercial restrictions in the Dify Open Source License. Easily deployed via Docker Compose. Dify Cloud provides a managed SaaS offering with free sandbox credits.

name: Flowise
description: Open-source drag-and-drop UI tool built on LangChain.js that enables developers to visually configure LLM chains, conversational agents, custom tool integrations, memory nodes, and vector database embeddings.
notes: MIT-licensed. Built using Node.js and React. Deploys as an independent container or npm package, exposing finished flows as embeddable chat widgets or REST API endpoints.

name: Langflow
subtype: Visual Framework for Multi-Agent & RAG Systems
description: Visual, Python-based web UI framework designed for prototyping and testing multi-agent workflows, custom prompt chains, and RAG architectures with live execution tracing and reusable component building blocks.
notes: Acquired by DataStax. MIT-licensed. Every visual block corresponds directly to Python code that developers can inspect, customize, and export into production applications.

name: n8n
subtype: Self-Hostable Workflow Automation with AI Agents
description: Fair-code workflow automation platform that integrates 400+ business applications with native LangChain AI nodes, enabling developers to build autonomous AI agents, chat triggers, and custom data sync pipelines.
notes: Source-available under Sustainable Use License (free for self-hosted internal business use). n8n Cloud offers managed tiers. AI Agent node supports conversational memory, tools, and sub-workflows.

name: LM Studio
description: Cross-platform desktop application for discovering, downloading, and running quantized LLMs (GGUF format) completely offline on macOS, Windows, and Linux, exposing a local OpenAI-compatible REST server.
notes: Free for personal use; commercial deployment requires LM Studio for Work license. Connects directly to Hugging Face to search and pull quantized model weights with automatic hardware GPU offloading.

name: LocalAI
description: Free, open-source drop-in replacement REST API compatible with OpenAI specifications for local and edge inference. Runs text generation, vision, audio transcription, image generation, and embeddings without requiring cloud connectivity.
notes: MIT-licensed. Built by Ettore Di Giacinto (mudler). Supports multiple backends including llama.cpp, Whisper.cpp, Diffusers, and ONNX inside standard Docker containers on consumer CPUs and GPUs.

name: Jan
subtype: Open-Source Offline Local AI Desktop Client
description: 100% open-source, privacy-first desktop application and local API server that runs LLMs locally on personal hardware. Stores all conversations, models, and embeddings locally on disk without telemetry tracking.
notes: AGPL-3.0 licensed. Developed by Menhir. Powered by the Nitro inference engine (C++). Exposes a local HTTP server at `http://localhost:1337` mimicking OpenAI chat endpoints for local development.

name: MLX
subtype: Machine Learning Framework for Apple Silicon
description: Efficient machine learning framework designed specifically for Apple Silicon by Apple machine learning research. Features unified memory architecture exploitation, multi-device array operations, and lazy evaluation for fast local inference.
notes: MIT-licensed. Uses Python and C++ APIs designed intentionally similar to NumPy and PyTorch. Powers `mlx-lm` for running high-parameter LLMs locally with high throughput on M1/M2/M3/M4 MacBooks.

name: DeepEval
subtype: Unit Testing & Evaluation Framework for LLM Apps
description: Open-source evaluation and unit testing framework for LLM applications. Provides production-grade metrics for evaluating hallucination, answer relevancy, faithfulness, G-Eval, and prompt injection defense within CI/CD pipelines.
notes: Apache 2.0 licensed. Designed to integrate directly with `pytest` for automated regression testing of prompt updates, model swaps, and retrieval adjustments. Confident AI provides cloud tracking dashboards.

name: Ragas
subtype: Automated Evaluation Framework for RAG Pipelines
description: Open-source framework tailored for evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems. Computes reference-free scores for context precision, context recall, faithfulness, and answer relevance to pinpoint retrieval versus generation failures.
notes: Apache 2.0 licensed. Developed by Exploding Gradients. Features synthetic test dataset generation capabilities using document corpuses to automate comprehensive RAG benchmark suites.

name: NeMo Guardrails
description: Open-source toolkit developed by NVIDIA for adding programmable guardrails to LLM conversational systems. Enforces topical boundaries, blocks jailbreak attempts, checks factual consistency, and prevents hallucinated statements using Colang scripts.
notes: Apache 2.0 licensed. Uses the modeling language Colang to define topical flows and dialog rules. Can run locally alongside any LLM (LangChain, LlamaIndex, LiteLLM) to govern input/output interactions before reaching end-users.

name: Claude Code
description: Anthropic's agentic command-line interface tool that operates directly in developer terminals. Reads entire local codebases, edits files across directories, runs terminal commands, and resolves complex git pull requests autonomously.
notes: Client runs locally as an interactive terminal CLI; requires an active Anthropic API key or cloud provider credentials (AWS Bedrock / Google Vertex AI) billed per token. Executes commands in user-approved terminal sessions.

name: Amazon Q Developer
description: Generative AI assistant built by Amazon Web Services for software development. Delivers code completions, automated code upgrades (such as Java version migrations), security vulnerability scanning, and AWS cloud architecture advice.
notes: Formerly Amazon CodeWhisperer. Free tier offers code suggestions and reference tracking. Pro tier ($19/user/month) adds code transformation agents, higher monthly chat limits, and centralized enterprise management.

name: Sourcegraph Cody
description: AI code assistant powered by Sourcegraph's code graph that understands entire multi-repository codebases. Provides codebase-aware autocomplete, inline refactoring, multi-file unit test generation, and deep semantic code search.
notes: Free Community plan available for individual developers. Pro ($9/month) and Enterprise ($19/user/month) plans unlock unlimited queries, custom multi-repo context indexing, and self-hosted backend connections.

name: Abridge
description: Generative AI clinical conversation platform that listens to doctor-patient medical encounters in real-time and automatically drafts structured, audit-ready clinical notes mapped directly into electronic health record (EHR) systems like Epic.
notes: Enterprise B2B healthcare contract pricing per clinician. Features linked evidence timestamps mapping every generated medical claim back to the original spoken audio snippet for clinician verification. HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II certified.

name: Hume AI
description: Conversational voice AI platform powered by an Empathic Voice Interface (EVI). Analyzes vocal inflections, pitch, pauses, and emotional nuances to engage in natural, emotionally responsive spoken interactions.
notes: Accessible via web playground and developer WebSocket API. Free tier offers introductory developer credits. Paid usage is metered per audio minute of real-time speech processing and expression analysis.

name: DeepL Translator
subtype: Neural Machine Translation & AI Writing Platform
description: Neural machine translation platform offering nuanced language translations across 30+ global languages. Preserves document layouts (PDF, Word, PowerPoint), adapts translations to custom company glossaries, and provides AI writing adjustments via DeepL Write.
notes: Free web translation without registration up to character limits. DeepL Pro plans ($8.74–$57.49/user/month) remove text limits, enforce zero-data-retention data privacy, and allow unlimited document translations. DeepL API billed separately.

name: Wordtune
description: AI writing companion developed by AI21 Labs that helps writers rephrase full sentences, adjust tone between casual and formal, summarize long reading materials, and generate contextual text completions across web editors.
notes: Free plan includes 10 rewrites per day. Plus plan ($9.99/month) and Unlimited plan ($14.99/month billed annually) grant unlimited rewrites, full paragraph restructuring, and document summaries.

name: Wondercraft
description: AI-powered audio workstation that turns written scripts, blogs, and notes into professional podcasts, audio advertisements, audiobooks, and meditations using hyper-realistic AI voices, royalty-free background music, and sound mixing.
notes: Free trial includes limited generation minutes with watermark. Creator ($29/month) and Pro ($89/month) plans offer higher audio minute allowances, voice cloning, RSS podcast hosting, and multi-track audio mixing.

name: InVideo AI
description: Generative video creation tool that converts prompt ideas into complete video presentations with scriptwriting, AI voiceover narration, stock video footage selection, subtitles, and music tracks ready for YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram.
notes: Free plan includes 10 minutes/week of AI generation with watermarked video exports. Plus ($20/month) and Max ($48/month) plans remove watermarks, unlock premium iStock assets, and allow voice cloning.

name: Captions
subtype: AI Creative Video Studio for Creators
description: AI-powered video recording and editing studio tailored for talking-head content creators. Features automatic dynamic animated captions, AI eye-contact correction, speech denoising, compression, and automated jump cuts.
notes: Mobile (iOS/Android) and desktop web application. Free trial available with limited exports. Pro subscription ($9.99/month or annual plans) unlocks unlimited AI eye-contact realignment, background music ducking, and 4K exports.

name: Recraft
description: Generative design tool engineered specifically for graphic designers. Generates editable vector graphics (SVG), 3D illustrations, pixel art, and brand iconography with strict brand color palette controls and infinite canvas layout.
notes: Free tier offers 50 daily credits with public generation gallery. Basic ($20/month) and Pro plans offer private generations, fast GPU generation modes, and full commercial ownership of vector outputs.

name: Photoroom
description: AI photo editing application designed for e-commerce entrepreneurs. Provides high-precision automated background removal, realistic AI-generated studio product backgrounds, batch image resizing, and shadow generation.
notes: Free tier allows standard background removals on mobile and web with Photoroom watermarks. Pro subscription ($9.99/month or $69.99/year) removes watermarks, adds HD cutouts, batch editing up to 50 images, and API access.

name: Granola
description: Meeting notepad for macOS that records system audio without requiring a bot to visibly join the meeting room. Combines human typed bullet notes with internal speech transcription to produce enriched, customizable meeting minutes.
notes: Desktop client captures internal computer audio locally without inviting third-party bot accounts into Google Meet, Zoom, or Slack calls. Free plan includes 25 meetings; Business plan ($10/month) offers unlimited meetings.

name: Read AI
description: Multi-platform meeting intelligence service that transcribes video calls, analyzes attendee engagement, tracks sentiment, flags conversational fatigue, and generates automated video highlights and recap emails across Zoom, Teams, and Meet.
notes: Free tier includes 5 meetings per month with standard metrics. Pro ($15/seat/month) and Enterprise plans offer unlimited meetings, video highlight reels, CRM integrations, and executive Chief-of-Staff briefing summaries.

name: Clay
subtype: AI-Powered Sales Prospecting & Data Enrichment Platform
description: Outbound sales platform that cascades data across 50+ providers to enrich lead records. Uses integrated LLMs (Claygent) to scrape company websites, research prospects, qualify leads, and generate personalized cold outreach emails at scale.
notes: Free tier includes 100 enrichment credits/month. Starter ($149/month), Explorer ($349/month), and Pro ($800/month) tiers grant scaled credit allowances for waterfall enrichment and automated AI web research actions.

name: Apollo AI
description: All-in-one B2B sales intelligence platform with a verified database of 275+ million contacts. Integrates AI-driven sales writing to craft personalized email sequences, score buyer intent, and record sales call insights.
notes: Free plan provides limited email credits and basic sequencing. Basic ($49/user/month), Professional ($79/user/month), and Organization tiers offer uncapped email sends, mobile direct dials, and AI meeting intelligence.

name: Sanas
description: Real-time speech-to-speech AI software for global contact centers. Modifies speaker accents in real-time on live voice calls to enhance intelligibility while preserving the speaker's vocal identity, emotional inflection, and tone.
notes: Enterprise B2B software running on agent desktop endpoints to ensure low-latency audio processing (<20ms). Designed to reduce customer friction and communication barriers in multilingual customer support operations.

name: OpenAI o3-mini
